text: In order to improve residents’ legal awareness, the present study evaluated the importance of enhancing public legal awareness in regulating deviant behavior from the perspective of social psychology. The research questions concerned whether the number of deviant incidents in the surveyed cities decreased after the implementation of legal education, whether the age distribution of the groups involved in deviant incidents changed, and whether public perceptions of the functions of law shifted toward the protection of rights and the performance of obligations. The study drew conclusions from a quantitative comparison of deviance incident records and from a survey of public perceptions conducted before and after the implementation of legal education, and the findings provide a theoretical and practical basis for improving public legal awareness and regulating deviant behavior.
source_label: Enhancing public legal awareness in regulating normative deviance: a social psychological evaluation of legal education
